summary: @servicetitan/carto-charts-react preinstall downloads Bun to execute obfuscated 727KB payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs downloads Bun v1.3.13 from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/<platform>.zip, unpacks it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it against the bundled math_init.js (or uses a locally-installed bun if present). math_init.js is a 727,680-byte single-line bundle marked '// @bun @bun-cjs' using string-array-shuffle obfuscation (WV8StW rotator, n7gIxM constant table, hc1jfK9 alphabet decoder) — the payload is not human-inspectable without deobfuscation. The advertised purpose is a small React wrapper over echarts-for-react (dist/index.js is ~1.5KB); the preinstall dropper and 727KB obfuscated payload bear no relation to that purpose. The @servicetitan scope is used, matching a ServiceTitan-internal-package impersonation shape. Bun's origin is legitimate (oven-sh releases), but its role here is to launder execution of the sibling obfuscated payload on the installer's machine at npm install time, bypassing tooling that only inspects Node-resolved code.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
